title: Cancellation of Vehicle Service Contracts: Reasons, Signed Requests and Effective Basis
content:
Under Vehicle Service Contracts, a service contract is cancelled before expiration for one of four reasons: the borrower's voluntary cancellation, the sale of the repossessed vehicle, a total loss of the vehicle, or the unwinding of the retail installment contract. A cancellation moves the service contract from active to cancelled.

## Voluntary cancellation by the borrower

A voluntary cancellation (cancellation reason borrower voluntary) is processed only under a cancellation request that the borrower has signed. The cancellation request must be signed no later than the plan's number of days a request stays open after the request was created. The signature period is counted in calendar days from the date part of the request's creation time, and a signature on the last day is in time; an unsigned request lapses.

Whether a request is signed, and when it was created and signed, is read from the cancellation request record.

| Hypothetical request created on 3 March, with a signature period of 10 calendar days | Result |
|---|---|
| Signed on 13 March (3 March plus 10 calendar days, the last day) | in time |
| Signed on 14 March | not in time |
| Never signed | the request lapses |

The creation time counts by its date part only: a request created late in the evening of 3 March has the same last day, 13 March, as one created that morning.

## Cancellation by the company

The company cancels without a request when the repossessed vehicle is sold (repossession sale), when the vehicle is a total loss (total loss) and when the retail installment contract is unwound (contract unwound); paying the contract off never cancels the service contract.

| Event | Cancels the service contract | Request from the borrower |
|---|---|---|
| Sale of the repossessed vehicle | Yes, by the company | not needed |
| Total loss of the vehicle | Yes, by the company | not needed |
| Retail installment contract unwound | Yes, by the company | not needed |
| Retail installment contract paid off | Never | — |

## Effective date and odometer

The effective date and odometer follow the plan's effective basis for the reason, mileage being measured on the odometer reading of that triggering record:

- borrower voluntary — the date and odometer on the signed request;
- repossession sale — the vehicle sale date and the odometer at recovery;
- total loss — the date of loss and the odometer on the insurer valuation;
- contract unwound — the retail installment contract's closed date and the odometer at sale.

## The cancellation record

The cancelled service contract shows status cancelled, the cancellation reason, the cancellation effective date by reason, the cancellation odometer at the effective date, and the processing date as its closed date.
